findings.description: AWS access key and secret access key are hardcoded in plaintext within the instance user_data script, which is visible via the EC2 metadata service and Terraform state, risking credential leakage.
Security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the instance to brute-force and unauthorized access attempts from the entire internet.
Security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0. While this may be intentional for a public web server, combined with unrestricted egress it broadens attack surface unnecessarily.
Security group allows all outbound traffic (all protocols/ports) to 0.0.0.0/0, which could facilitate data exfiltration if the instance is compromised.
Subnet has map_public_ip_on_launch set to true, causing instances launched here to automatically receive public IP addresses, increasing exposure to the internet.
Subnet has map_public_ip_on_launch set to true, causing instances launched here to automatically receive public IP addresses, increasing exposure to the internet.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, meaning data at rest on this volume is not encrypted.
The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs does not have server-side encryption configured, leaving sensitive network traffic logs unencrypted at rest.

findings.issue_category: missing access controls / public access block
findings.description: The S3 bucket has no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, and force_destroy is enabled, risking unauthorized access or accidental deletion of flow log data.
